mauritius.overview: Mauritius offers solid day hiking anchored by Black River Gorges National Park and the dramatic Le Morne Brabant peninsula. Walkers can explore the forested trails to Black River Peak or tackle the steep, rocky scramble up Le Morne, where a guide is recommended, for sweeping views of the Indian Ocean. The best conditions run from May to October, avoiding the heavy rains that make the steep rock routes dangerous.

months.1: Cyclone risk and heavy rains make this a poor time for steep trails. The rock scramble on Le Morne is dangerous when wet, leaving only lower forest paths walkable.
months.2: Rain and cyclone risk continue, and wet rock makes the Le Morne scramble unsafe. Lower, flatter forest paths in Black River Gorges are the realistic option.
months.5: Cooler, drier weather brings the best conditions of the year. The steep rock scramble up Le Morne is dry, and the forest trails to Black River Peak give clear views over the island.
months.6: Dry, cool days continue, with the Le Morne scramble firm underfoot and good visibility from Black River Peak.
months.7: Settled dry weather keeps both the Le Morne scramble and the Black River Gorges forest trails in good condition.
months.8: Cool, dry conditions hold, making this an excellent month for the long forest trails of Black River Gorges.
months.9: Dry weather and mild temperatures continue, with the rock on Le Morne safe to scramble and views clear over the island and ocean.
months.10: Dry conditions last through most of the month, though warmth builds, so early starts suit the Le Morne scramble.

mendoza.overview: Mendoza is the gateway to the high Andes and Aconcagua Provincial Park, which requires an entry permit. Walkers drive into the mountains for long day hikes to viewpoints like the Confluencia camp, or take multi-day treks toward the base camps of the highest peak outside Asia. The terrain is stark, with glacier valleys and colorful rock. The best walking is from December to March, when the high trails are clear of snow.

months.1: The high Andes are clear of snow, making this prime time for the day hike to Confluencia or multi-day treks toward the Aconcagua base camps.
months.2: Stable conditions continue on the trails to Confluencia and toward the Aconcagua base camps, with the stark high-altitude scenery fully accessible.
months.12: Warmer days clear the last snow from the high trails, opening the Confluencia day hike and the base camp routes.
months.6: Deep snow closes the high Andes to walkers. Hiking is restricted to simple low-elevation walks in the foothills, in chilly weather.
months.7: The high mountains stay closed under snow. Only short foothill walks near Mendoza are practical.
months.10: The walking season starts to open up as snow clears from the middle elevations. The Confluencia day hike often becomes accessible, while higher treks hold snow.

mexicocity.overview: Mexico City has access to high-altitude trails and forested day hikes just beyond the urban sprawl. The main draw for serious hikers is the demanding walk-up of Iztaccíhuatl, a 17,160-foot dormant volcano that requires acclimatization but no technical gear on its standard route. Closer to town, the pine-oak forests of Desierto de los Leones provide gentler loops.

months.1: The dry winter weather provides clear skies and excellent visibility for the demanding ascent of Iztaccíhuatl, though temperatures at high elevations are freezing.
months.10: The weather stabilizes as the dry season returns, offering some of the best conditions for the demanding nine-mile round trip on Iztaccíhuatl.

milford-sound-fiordland.overview: Fiordland holds famous multi-day treks that lead walkers through glacier-carved valleys, dense rainforest, and alpine passes to the steep walls of the fjords. The Milford, Routeburn, and Kepler tracks are the main draws, requiring advance hut bookings in the Great Walks season. Day hikers can tackle sections of these routes or steep climbs like the Routeburn Shelter to Key Summit, earning views of the Darran Mountains and hanging valleys. The region is wet, so expect rain and waterfalls at any time of year.

months.2: February offers excellent conditions for the multi-day treks and day hikes. The alpine passes are clear of snow, and the long daylight hours allow for extended days on the trail.
months.6: Snow closes the alpine sections of the Routeburn and Kepler tracks. Walking is restricted to short, low-level forest paths, and the Milford Road may face avalanche closures.
months.11: The multi-day treks are fully operational, and the alpine passes are generally clear of snow. Waterfalls are at their most spectacular as the snowmelt combines with the region's frequent rain.

months.1: The Mongolian winter brings deep snow and extreme sub-zero temperatures, and the trails are out of reach.
months.2: Deep snow and severe cold persist, and walking routes stay out of reach.
months.12: Winter settles in with deep snow and extreme cold, keeping the trails closed to walkers.
months.7: Warm days and long daylight make this the main trekking window, with the Gorkhi-Terelj valleys green and the western routes open.
months.8: Clear trails continue in Gorkhi-Terelj and across the western routes, with cooler nights arriving late in the month.

monterey-big-sur.overview: Monterey and Big Sur offer dramatic coastal hiking where trails trace ocean cliffs and drop into deep redwood canyons. Day hikers explore the rocky coves of Point Lobos State Natural Reserve and the steep, ocean-facing ridges of Garrapata State Park. Inland routes climb through shaded groves of old-growth coast redwoods in the Santa Lucia Mountains. The mild climate allows year-round walking, though winter storms bring mud and road closures.

morocco.overview: The High Atlas Mountains offer dramatic walking within a few hours' reach of the city. The centerpiece is the two-day trek up Mount Toubkal, a 13,670-foot summit reached from the village of Imlil that rewards walkers with sweeping views over the rugged peaks and valleys. Lower trails wind through terraced Berber villages and walnut groves for long day hikes. The best conditions run from March to May and September to November, avoiding the intense mid-year heat and late-year snows.

months.3: Snow begins to melt on the middle elevations, opening up longer day hikes. The Mount Toubkal trek may still hold icy patches requiring caution.
months.9: Temperatures begin to drop, bringing excellent walking conditions back to the High Atlas. The skies are very clear, offering great views from the Mount Toubkal summit.
